prompt: A scooter app charges $y = 2 + 0.15m$ dollars for a ride of $m$ minutes. How many dollars do you pay before riding a single minute ($m = 0$)?
hint: Before you ride at all, the number of minutes is zero. What part of the cost is left then?

hints.text: Before you ride at all, the number of minutes is zero. What part of the cost is left then?
Put $m = 0$ into the formula to get $y = 2 + 0.15 \times 0$. Anything times zero is zero.
$y = 2 + 0 = 2$, so you pay $2$ dollars before riding a single minute.

explanation: Substitute $m = 0$ into the formula, since no minutes have been ridden: $y = 2 + 0.15 \times 0 = 2$.
The $2$ is the $y$-intercept of the line. It is the starting fee you pay to unlock the scooter no matter how long you ride.
So the cost at zero minutes is $2$ dollars. The $0.15$ is the slope, the extra cost for each minute.

alternativeExplanations.title: Start-then-move
steps: Every $y = mx + b$ story splits into a start and a move.
Here the start is $\$2$ (unlock) and the move is $\$0.15$ each minute; at zero minutes only the start is charged.
